fullPassage: There's a saying that "you can't eat information." That may be so, but the food we eat today is the fruit of thousands of years of increasingly high-quality information — the knowledge of how to farm — what seeds, what tools and how to use them, what times of year, what irrigation, what sequence of one crop after another on the same land. What we eat is solar energy, filtered, concentrated, and distilled through the lens of human knowledge. The energy the Earth receives from the sun each year has remained more or less constant through all of human civilization. What's allowed us to flourish is our increasingly sophisticated knowledge of how to capture an ever-growing but still tiny fraction of that energy in a form that can fuel our bodies. Every step in the advancement of our knowledge has brought with it an increase in the amount of energy we can tap into.

questions.passage: There's a saying that "you can't eat information." That may be so, but the food we eat today is the fruit of thousands of years of increasingly high-quality information — the knowledge of how to farm — what seeds, what tools and how to use them, what times of year, what irrigation, what sequence of one crop after another on the same land. What we eat is solar energy, filtered, concentrated, and distilled through the lens of human knowledge. The energy the Earth receives from the sun each year has remained more or less constant through all of human civilization. What's allowed us to flourish is our increasingly sophisticated knowledge of how to capture an ever-growing but still tiny fraction of that energy in a form that can fuel our bodies. Every step in the advancement of our knowledge has brought with it __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: an increase in the amount of energy we can tap into

det.korean: 지식의 진보는 우리가 활용할 수 있는 에너지의 양의 증가를 가져왔다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② an increase in the amount of energy we can tap into: 원문 일치
❌ ① decrease in resources: 자원 감소, 반대
❌ ③ reduction in population: 인구 감소, 무관
❌ ④ decline in productivity: 생산성 감소, 반대
det.tip: tap into(활용하다) — 지식이 발전할수록 활용 가능한 에너지가 증가한다는 핵심 주장

a diminishing share of global resources

det.korean: 점점 커지지만 여전히 작은 그 에너지의 일부를 포착하는 것.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ an ever-growing but still tiny fraction of that energy: 원문 일치 — 태양 에너지의 점점 커지지만 여전히 작은 부분
❌ ① entirety(전체): tiny fraction과 모순
❌ ② artificial sources(인공 에너지원): solar energy와 모순
❌ ④ diminishing share(줄어드는 몫): ever-growing과 모순
det.tip: ever-growing but still tiny fraction — 에너지 활용량은 늘어나지만 태양 전체 에너지에 비하면 여전히 극소량
